label: ai-generated
title: Transformations: health, science and the media

items.sentence1: The scientist had no idea at the time how important her discovery would turn out to be.
items.after: how important her discovery would turn out to be.

explanation.en: Part 1: the negative adverbial 'little' at the front of the clause causes inversion with the auxiliary 'did'. Part 2: the subject comes after 'did', and the verb is in the base form: 'the scientist realise', not 'realised'. 'She' cannot replace 'the scientist', because nobody has been named yet.
explanation.cs: Část 1: záporné příslovce little na začátku věty vyžaduje inverzi s pomocným did. Část 2: za did následuje podmět a sloveso v základním tvaru: the scientist realise (ne realised). Zájmeno she nelze použít, osoba ještě nebyla zmíněna.

items.sentence1: The clinic has no flu vaccines left.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'has no ... left' is the present result of a past process, so the present perfect phrasal verb 'has run out' is used ('run' is also the past participle). Part 2: 'run out' needs 'of' before the thing that is finished.
explanation.cs: Část 1: 'has no … left' je výsledek v přítomnosti, proto předpřítomný čas frázového slovesa: has run out (příčestí run). Část 2: run out se pojí s of před tím, co došlo: run out of vaccines.

items.sentence1: I definitely sent the patient's notes to the hospital; I can picture myself doing it.
items.after: the patient's notes to the hospital.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'definitely ... I can picture myself' becomes a strong memory, 'clearly remember'. Part 2: 'remember' + -ing ('sending' or 'having sent') refers to a memory of an earlier action. 'Remember to send' means 'not forget to do it' and changes the meaning.
explanation.cs: Část 1: jistotu a živou vzpomínku vyjádříme clearly / distinctly remember. Část 2: remember + -ing (sending, having sent) = pamatuji si, že jsem to udělal. 'Remember to send' znamená 'nezapomenout to udělat', to je jiný význam.

items.sentence1: Since I moved abroad, I have had no contact with my old school friends.
fullAnswers: have been out of touch with
have not been in touch with
have not kept in touch with
have not stayed in touch with

explanation.en: Part 1: 'have had no contact' becomes a fixed phrase with 'touch' in the present perfect: 'have lost touch' (or 'have not kept / been in touch'). Part 2: all these phrases take the preposition 'with' before the person.
explanation.cs: Část 1: 'have had no contact' nahradíme ustáleným spojením s touch v předpřítomném čase: have lost touch (ztratit kontakt) nebo have not kept / been in touch. Část 2: tato spojení se pojí s předložkou with.

items.sentence1: The documentary was so moving that many viewers wrote to the channel.
items.after: that many viewers wrote to the channel.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'so + adjective + that' becomes 'such + a + adjective + noun + that'; the article 'a' is needed because 'documentary' is a singular countable noun. Part 2: the adjective comes before the noun, 'moving documentary'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: so + přídavné jméno + that se mění na such + a + přídavné jméno + podstatné jméno + that; člen a je nutný, protože documentary je počitatelné v jednotném čísle. Část 2: přídavné jméno stojí před podstatným: moving documentary.

items.sentence1: We were disappointed that so few people came to the clinic's open day.

explanation.en: Part 1: the clause 'so few people came' becomes a noun phrase, 'low (or poor) turnout'. 'Few turnout' is wrong, because 'turnout' collocates with low, poor or small. Part 2: 'turnout' is followed by 'at' or 'for' before the event.
explanation.cs: Část 1: větu 'so few people came' převedeme na podstatné jméno: low / poor turnout (nízká účast). 'Few turnout' nelze, turnout se pojí s low, poor, small. Část 2: před akcí stojí předložka at nebo for.
